summary.name: Xtreme Download Manager (XDM)
summary.one_liner: XDM is a free, open-source download manager for Windows, macOS and Linux that speeds up downloads, resumes broken transfers, and saves streaming videos from the browser.
keywords: free download manager windows mac linux
use_cases: Resume a download after a crash or lost connection
Save streaming videos from a website
Batch download many links from a page
Cap download speed to free bandwidth
summary.what_it_does: XDM runs as a native desktop app alongside the browser and takes over downloads through a browser extension for Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Brave, Opera and Vivaldi. It splits files into several parallel connections and rebalances them to use available bandwidth. It detects HLS (.m3u8) and DASH (.mpd) streams while video plays, lets the user pick a quality, and merges separate audio and video into one file. It can resume interrupted downloads, refresh expired links, batch download links from a page or pasted list, and schedule downloads with a global speed limiter.
notable: Native app with no Electron or embedded browser, idling at about 30 MB memory on Windows per the page
Saves HLS and DASH streaming video and merges audio and video
Free and open source under the GNU GPL, source on GitHub
Native builds for Windows x64/ARM64, Mac Apple silicon and Intel, Linux x86-64/ARM64
caveats: Page URL has moved: the page title says it was moved to https://xdmweb.github.io/
Video saving and other features depend on the browser extension being installed
Some expired or session-bound links may need the Refresh link feature or fail to resume, per the error guides listed
